title: epochal-prefill-consolidator-and-entropy-aware-decode-scheduler
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Prefill-decode handoff continues to be a major driver of tail latency for long-context workloads. We observed oscillating KV cache prefetch patterns and redundant prefill work across microbatches which inflate kernel contention and increase cost. This change introduces an "epochal prefill consolidator" that groups closely-timed prefill work into short-lived epochs and a complementary "entropy-aware decode scheduler" that biases decode kernel placement to minimize KV cache thrashing.

Motivation: Existing speculative prefill flows operate per-request or per-microbatch and can cause duplicate KV priming when many requests share prefixes or similar attention windows. By introducing epoch-level aggregation we reduce duplicate kernel work, enable per-epoch KV prewarming (single warmup per working set), and give the scheduler better signals to reduce cross-epoch eviction.

Design summary: 1) Epochal prefill consolidator: a lightweight coordinator that opens a short time window (configurable, default 6ms) and merges prefill intents into a single consolidated prefill op when affinities (model version, seq length, prefix hash) match. Consolidator emits a single prefill token map and an epoch id that callers use to associate decode requests. 2) Entropy-aware decode scheduler: a scoring function that uses per-epoch entropy (diversity of prefix hashes, KV hit-rate estimate, and kernel queue depth) to bias decode kernels to nodes with warmer KV caches and lower eviction risk. 3) Per-epoch KV prewarming: when consolidation produces a prefill, a single accelerated KV warm path is invoked that registers the epoch id to the KV cache to prevent soft-evictions for the epoch lifetime. 4) Backwards-compatibility: all new components are opt-in behind runtime flags and fall back to existing per-microbatch prefill if disabled.

What changed (high level): - New epochal consolidator module and API surface (src/runtime/prefill/epochal_consolidator.*) - Entropy-based scheduler hooks and scoring (src/runtime/scheduler/entropy_scheduler.*) - Per-epoch KV prewarmer with lifecycle management (src/runtime/kv/kv_prewarmer.*) - Metrics and tracing additions for epoch boundaries and consolidation rate (docs/observability/prefill-metrics.md; src/runtime/README-prefill.md) - Integration tests and microbench harness (tests/integration/prefill_epochal_test.py; examples/perf/epochal-bench.yaml)

Checklist: - [x] Consolidator implementation - [x] Scheduler integration - [x] KV prewarming lifecycle - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Observability (histograms for epoch size, consolidation ratio, epoch lifetime) - [x] Canary rollout plan documented

Testing: Unit tests for consolidator logic and scheduler scoring added. Integration test simulates 1000 concurrent short-prefill requests with synthetic prefix collisions. Benchmarks run on perf lab GPUs show consistent p99 tail reduction and cost-per-token improvements.

Rollout: Feature flag off by default. Gradual canary (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) across hosting and dedicated clusters with extra tracing enabled during canary. If KV eviction warning rate rises by >5% during canary, auto-rollback is triggered.
commits: init: add epochal consolidator core and interfaces; scheduler: add entropy scoring and advisories; kv: implement prewarmer lifecycle and registration; metrics: add epoch metrics and dashboard artifacts; tests: add epochal integration harness; docs: document flags and rollout steps

review_comments: Rafiq: Nice approach — consolidating prefill windows should cut duplicated kernel work. Two asks: add guardrails for memory blowups when an epoch accumulates too many intents, and ensure the prewarm pin uses soft pins so the cache can still evict under pressure.
Maya: Added epoch size cap (configurable, default 128 intents) and changed prewarm to soft-pin semantics. Also added metrics to track soft-pin evictions.
Ellen: Scheduler scoring looks good but the entropy formula needs calibration. Can we add an experiment flag to toggle entropyWeight and collect per-epoch hit/miss stats?
Maya: Added runtime flag --prefill-entropy-weight and instrumented per-epoch hit/miss counters. Updated tests to validate scoring range.

Diego: Integration test failure on initial run — saw intermittent flakiness in perf harness. Root cause: race in epoch close path.
Maya: Fixed by making epoch close atomic and added a small jitter to close window to avoid thundering herd. Re-ran and green.
release_notes: Introduce epochal prefill consolidation and entropy-aware decode scheduling. Opt-in feature (runtime flag). Expected improvements: fewer duplicate prefill kernels, reduced KV thrashing, improved tail latency and lower cost per token. Rollout gated and observable.
rollout_plan: Feature flag default off. Canary to 1% of traffic for 24h with elevated tracing -> 10% for 48h -> 50% for 72h -> 100%. Metric gates: p99 tail, KV eviction rate, consolidation ratio. Automatic rollback if KV eviction rate increases >5% or p99 regresses >10%.
notes: This PR focuses on runtime-level consolidation and scheduler hints; it does not change model kernels themselves. Follow-ups planned: GPU-side kernel hinting for better co-location and adding per-epoch persisted statistics for long-running Dedicated clusters.
